title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: US markets were closed over the weekend; Friday's close left the S&P 500, Dow and Nasdaq at fresh records after a strong week, with Samsung/TSMC earnings pointing to a firm reopen Monday.

Markets: Oil stayed elevated (Brent ~$104) after a reported supertanker explosion from a naval mine in the Strait of Hormuz sent freight costs to records, even as Trump pledged no Iran strike before the midterms.

Companies: Samsung posted a record ~$80B quarterly profit on the AI-memory boom and TSMC's Q3 revenue jumped 51%, underscoring AI chip demand ahead of next week's bank-earnings slate (JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, BlackRock start Tuesday).

Companies: OpenAI's annualized revenue is now pegged at $50B, about $20B below earlier reports; Anthropic launched a Critical Infrastructure Defense Program (with Accenture, CrowdStrike, Deloitte, Palo Alto Networks) to help secure power/water/grid systems against AI-enabled cyberattacks.
Companies: Microsoft was briefly suspended from a key foreign-worker green-card program by the Trump administration, then had CEO Satya Nadella honored with a national innovation medal hours later.

Macro/Policy: Political pressure on the Fed is building — Trump plans a White House hearing on Fed governor Lisa Cook — ahead of next week's September CPI (Wed) and PPI (Thu) and the Fed's Beige Book.

Macro/Policy: Europe is a growing worry: the French OAT-Bund spread is lingering near post-financial-crisis highs, and a Bundesbank official warned the risk of a European debt crisis has risen sharply.

Macro/Policy: The Financial Stability Board said most major economies are unprepared for a large bank failure (only the US, UK, Japan and Hong Kong passed), while the NY Fed reviews banks' private-credit exposure amid fee lawsuits against BDCs (FS KKR, Blue Owl, Ares).
Macro/Policy: Crypto regulation moved on two fronts — FinCEN withdrew its proposed rule targeting crypto mixers, and the SEC proposed a framework letting advisers custody cryptocurrencies.
